newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to threaten fines over KLM/Northwest deal data.
newsitem.headline: EU to threaten fines over KLM/Northwest deal data.

text.p: The European Commission is due on Wednesday to threaten Dutch airline KLM and possibly its American partner Northwest Airlines with daily fines if they fail to provide it with data on their alliance, a European Commission official told Reuters.
Sources said it was not clear whether Northwest would be subject to the fines.

"Tomorrow, the Commission will have taken a decision that if KLM and Northwest have not given the information which is required, the Commission will start fining them on a daily basis," the official said.

"The Commission is to give them a reasonable deadline, of a few days, to provide the information. It is simply an indication that the Commission is serious about investigating the other alliances," said the official, who asked not to be named.
Neither the official nor a second Commission source were able to clarify whether KLM or both airlines would face fines.
In Amsterdam, KLM said it was in talks with the Commission and added that fines were not yet at issue.

"KLM was approached by the European Commission as part of its investigation into airline alliances and is currently in talks with the European Commission on that...we have not received a formal decision from the EU," spokeswoman Marjolein Wenting said.

The Commission announced anti-trust probes into six North Atlantic airline alliances last July, including the one between KLM and Northwest and the proposed link-up between British Airways and AMR Corp 's American Airlines.

The second source said KLM had "showed some reluctance in providing us with the information", adding: "The amount is not important...But it shows that the Commission treats everybody in an equal way and that it is not only going for BA/American".

News of possible fines comes amid criticism from British Airways that the Commission has unfairly singled out its planned alliance with American and has ignored a string of other transatlantic tie-ups.

The Commission published three legal notices last October detailing its thinking on BA/American plans and on existing agreements between Delta Air Lines, Sabena, Swissair and Austrian Airlines, and between Lufthansa, United Airlines and Scandinavian Airlines System.

The official said British Airways's alliance with USAir was viewed as not worth investigating given that it was unlikely to last and added that work was underway on Air France's planned code-sharing partnerships with Continental Airlines and Delta.

While the Commission is due to report on the effects of airline alliances some time in March, the EU executive has already warned Britain against approving the BA/American as it stands, with Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert saying concessions offered by the airlines were insufficent.
